mainTopic: Who may judge a חליצה, which shoe is used for חליצה, and what exactly counts as removing it.
overview: The amud opens with who may serve as a judge. By תורה law a גר may judge a fellow גר. One whose mother is a born Jew may judge anyone. For חליצה, both parents must be born Jews. Next come two reports in רב's name: even אליהו could not cancel the people's custom of doing חליצה with a סנדל. The reports differ on whether a soft מנעל may be used לכתחילה, and the גמרא shows this is an older dispute among תנאים. The view that forbids a מנעל לכתחילה is explained as a rabbinic decree, out of concern for a torn shoe or a half shoe. רב then prefers a tight sandal, and an extra strap is tied on so the חליצה is done in the best way. רב rules that once most of the heel is out, the יבמה is free, and the גמרא shows that a ברייתא about 'most of the foot' means the same thing. That ברייתא also supports רבי ינאי: the woman must both untie and remove the shoe herself. The amud ends with questions about tearing or burning the shoe and about two shoes worn one over the other, which turn on whether חליצה means removing the shoe or uncovering the foot.

steps.title: A convert may judge a fellow convert
steps.stepSummary: By תורה law a גר may judge another גר. The פסוק requires a leader 'from among your brothers' only when he rules over born Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: By Torah law, a convert may judge his fellow convert. The verse says: 'You shall set a king over you … from among your brothers.' The requirement of 'from among your brothers' applies only when ruling 'over you' (born Jews). A convert judging a fellow convert is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule: a גר is allowed to be a judge for another גר, and it proves this from a פסוק about appointing a king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a king (and any official) must be 'from among your brothers,' which means a born Jew. The גמרא reads the word 'עָלֶיךָ' (over you) as limiting this. The rule applies only when the official rules over born Jews. When a גר judges other גרים, he is one of 'their brothers,' so the requirement does not block him.

keyTerms.meaning: From among your brothers, meaning a born Jew
Over you, meaning ruling over born Jews

phrases.aramaic: גֵּר דָּן אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ דְּבַר תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: A convert may judge his fellow by Torah law,
as it is stated: "You shall surely set a king over you
whom the Lord your God shall choose;
from among your brothers you shall set a king over you."
It is for "over you" that we require "from among your brothers,"
phrases.notes: Only when someone rules over born Jews must he himself be a born Jew.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל גֵּר דָּן אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ גֵּר.
phrases.english: but a convert may judge his fellow convert.

steps.triggerLanguage: גֵּר דָּן אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ דְּבַר תּוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section with the basic rule about a גר serving as a judge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By תורה law a גר may judge a fellow גר, because 'from among your brothers' is required only when ruling over born Jews.

steps.title: A convert with a Jewish mother may judge anyone
steps.stepSummary: If the גר's mother was a born Jew, he may judge even born Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if his mother was from Israel, he may judge even a born Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a further case: someone whose mother was born Jewish may judge even born Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 limited a גר to judging other גרים. Here the גמרא widens the permission. Having a Jewish-born mother is enough to count as 'from among your brothers,' so this person may judge all of ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: His mother is a born Jew

phrases.english: And if his mother was from Israel,
he may judge even a born Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הָיְתָה אִמּוֹ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands step 1's rule to a person with a Jewish-born mother.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One whose mother is a born Jew may judge even born Jews.

steps.title: For חליצה, both parents must be born Jews
steps.stepSummary: A judge for חליצה must have both a Jewish-born father and a Jewish-born mother, based on the פסוק 'and his name shall be called in Israel.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But for חליצה, he may not judge unless both his father and his mother are from Israel, as it says: 'And his name shall be called in Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets a stricter rule just for חליצה: the judge must have two Jewish-born parents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ordinary judging, a Jewish-born mother is enough (step 2). חליצה is an exception with a higher standard. The phrase 'בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל' in the חליצה פסוק is read to mean the judges must be fully of Jewish lineage, from both father and mother. This does not remove such a person from being a valid judge in general. It only adds an extra requirement for חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony of removing the shoe, which frees a יבמה from יבום
And his name shall be called in Israel

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels. A גר may judge a fellow גר. One with a Jewish-born mother may judge anyone. For חליצה, both parents must be born Jews.

phrases.english: But with regard to חליצה,
he may not judge unless his father and his mother are from Israel,
as it is stated: "And his name shall be called in Israel."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְעִנְיַן חֲלִיצָה עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 2: a Jewish mother is not enough for חליצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge for חליצה must have both a Jewish-born father and a Jewish-born mother.

steps.title: If אליהו permits a soft shoe, we listen; but the sandal stays
steps.stepSummary: רבה reports in the name of רב: if אליהו said a מנעל may be used for חליצה, we would accept it. If he said a סנדל may not be used, we would not accept it, because the people's custom is to use a סנדל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רב כהנא in the name of רב: If אליהו comes and says, 'We may do חליצה with a soft shoe,' we listen to him. If he says, 'We may not do חליצה with a sandal,' we do not listen to him, because the people already have the practice of using a sandal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new topic: which shoe is used for חליצה. It brings a statement from רב about how much weight a ruling from אליהו would carry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, אליהו could add the soft shoe (מנעל) as a valid option, and we would accept that. He could not take away the sandal (סנדל), because the people's settled custom already relies on it. Custom here is strong enough that even a prophet's word would not overturn it.

keyTerms.meaning: The people have the practice, an established custom

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two shoes. מנעל is the soft shoe, and סנדל is the sandal the people already use. Both reports agree about the סנדל; they differ only about the מנעל.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabba said that Rav Kahana said that Rav said:
If Elijah should come and say:
"One may perform חליצה with a soft shoe," we listen to him.
But if he says "One may not perform חליצה with a sandal," we do not listen to him,
for the people have already established the practice of using a sandal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַב: אִם יָבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ וְיֹאמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: what footwear is used for חליצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ruling from אליהו that permits a מנעל would be accepted. A ruling that forbids the סנדל would not be accepted, because of established custom.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how strong an established custom (מנהג) is in חליצה: even אליהו could not cancel it.

steps.title: A different report: if אליהו forbids the soft shoe, we listen
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reports the same teaching from רב differently: if אליהו said a מנעל may NOT be used, we would accept it. The סנדל part stays the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said in the name of רב כהנא in the name of רב: If אליהו comes and says, 'We may not do חליצה with a soft shoe,' we listen to him. If he says, 'We may not do חליצה with a sandal,' we do not listen to him, because the people already have the practice of using a sandal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of רב's statement that differs on the soft shoe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבה's version (step 4), אליהו would permit the מנעל. In רב יוסף's version, אליהו would forbid it, and we would still accept that. The two versions match on the סנדל: the people's custom cannot be overturned. The open question between them is whether a מנעל is valid for חליצה.
steps.whatToRemember: Both reports agree that the סנדל, backed by the people's custom, can never be ruled out. They disagree on whether אליהו would allow or forbid the מנעל.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said that Rav Kahana said that Rav said:
If Elijah should come and say:
"One may not perform חליצה with a soft shoe," we listen to him.
But if he says "One may not perform חליצה with a sandal," we do not listen to him,
for the people have already established the practice of using a sandal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A competing report of the same statement from רב, differing only on the מנעל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ruling from אליהו that forbids a מנעל would be accepted. A ruling that forbids the סנדל would not, because of custom.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רבה's and רב יוסף's versions of רב's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two versions of רב's teaching from Steps 4 and 5. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree that a סנדל is fine and that the custom is to use one. They differ only on what אליהו might say about a מנעל, so the גמרא wants to know whether that difference changes anything in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? (What practical result separates the two views?)

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the two versions of רב's teaching, from רבה and from רב יוסף.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the two versions in Steps 4 and 5 differ in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between רבה's and רב יוסף's versions of רב's statement.

steps.title: The difference: using a soft leather shoe from the start
steps.stepSummary: The two versions differ on whether a מנעל may be used for חליצה לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is whether a soft leather shoe may be used from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two versions disagree about whether you may plan from the start to do חליצה with a מנעל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבה's version, we would accept אליהו if he PERMITTED a מנעל. That means right now it is not used לכתחילה. In רב יוסף's version, we would accept אליהו if he FORBADE a מנעל. That means right now it is allowed even לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start; what you may plan to do
A soft leather shoe (different from the hard סנדל)

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions agree that a חליצה already done with a מנעל is valid. They disagree only about whether you may choose to use one from the start.

phrases.english: The difference between them is a soft leather shoe from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבה: a מנעל is not used לכתחילה. רב יוסף: a מנעל may be used even לכתחילה.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה's wording 'she did חליצה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's lenient view, because the משנה's past-tense wording suggests a מנעל is valid only after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says it is allowed even from the start: didn't we learn in the משנה, 'If she did חליצה with a soft leather shoe, her חליצה is valid'? That means after the fact, yes; from the start, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the view that a מנעל is fine even לכתחילה, using the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'if she DID חליצה' in the past tense. That kind of wording usually means 'if it already happened, it works'. That suggests a מנעל is only good בדיעבד, which goes against רב יוסף's version.

keyTerms.meaning: After the fact; once it has already been done

phrases.english: And according to the one who says even from the start,
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף's version, which allows a מנעל even from the start.

phrases.english: but didn't we learn: If she did חליצה with a soft leather shoe, her חליצה is valid.
After the fact, yes; from the start, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֲפִילּוּ לְכַתְּחִלָּה, וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the lenient side of the difference stated in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's version, which allows a מנעל לכתחילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה uses past-tense wording ('she did'), which suggests the act is valid only בדיעבד.

steps.title: The משנה's wording just matches its next clause
steps.stepSummary: A מנעל really is allowed even לכתחילה. The משנה used after-the-fact wording only to match its next clause, where an אנפיליא is invalid even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true even from the start. But since the משנה wanted to teach in the next part that with a cloth shoe her חליצה is invalid even after the fact, it also taught the first part in after-the-fact wording.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יוסף's view by explaining why the משנה used past-tense wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second clause, about an אנפיליא, really does need after-the-fact wording: even if it was already done, it does not count. To keep both clauses parallel, the משנה phrased the first clause the same way. So the wording does not prove that a מנעל is forbidden לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because (it wanted to keep the wording matching)
Last part / first part of a משנה
A soft shoe or sock made of cloth

steps.whatToRemember: Sometimes a משנה uses 'after the fact' wording only to match a nearby clause. That wording alone does not prove something is forbidden from the start.

phrases.english: The same is true even from the start.
But since it wanted to teach in the last part
that with a cloth shoe her חליצה is invalid, even after the fact,
it also taught the first part in after-the-fact wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ לְכַתְּחִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the wording as a matter of style: the first clause was phrased to match the second.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The past-tense wording shows that a מנעל is only valid בדיעבד.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מנעל is allowed even לכתחילה; the wording only parallels the אנפיליא clause.

steps.title: This question is already a dispute among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that whether a מנעל may be used לכתחילה is already disputed by תנאים. This sets up a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a soft leather shoe from the start is a dispute among the תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states that the question of using a מנעל לכתחילה is an older disagreement among the תנאים. It is setting up a ברייתא that will show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves the disagreement between רבה and רב יוסף back to the earlier generation of the תנאים. The proof is in the ברייתא that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among תנאים (the sages of the משנה era)

phrases.english: And a soft leather shoe from the start is a dispute among the תנאים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנְעָל לְכַתְּחִלָּה תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places the difference from Step 7 within an earlier dispute among תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether a מנעל may be used לכתחילה for חליצה is disputed by תנאים.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's visit to נציבין begins
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי יוסי met an elder in נציבין who knew רבי יהודה בן בתירא well, and asked whether he had ever seen him conduct a חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי יוסי said: Once I went to נציבין and found an elder. I asked him, 'Do you know רבי יהודה בן בתירא?' He said, 'Yes, he often eats at my table.' I asked, 'Did you ever see him conduct a חליצה for a יבמה?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the ברייתא that proves the dispute among תנאים. This part only sets up the story; the answer about the shoe comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי makes sure the elder knew רבי יהודה בן בתירא personally, so his eyewitness report can be trusted. The question about seeing a חליצה leads to what kind of shoe was used.

phrases.english: As it is taught: רבי יוסי said:
Once I went to נציבין,
and I found a certain elder.
I said to him: Do you know
רבי יהודה בן בתירא?
He said to me: Yes,
and he is often at my table.
Did you ever see him conduct the חליצה of a יבמה?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the ברייתא that supports the claim in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That using a מנעל לכתחילה is disputed among תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording רבי יוסי's conversation in נציבין about רבי יהודה בן בתירא's practice.

steps.title: The elder says a soft shoe is never used for חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The elder answers that he saw רבי יהודה בן בתירא do חליצה many times. When רבי יוסי asks whether he used a מנעל or a סנדל, the elder says no one does חליצה with a מנעל at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: I saw him do חליצה many times. I asked: with a soft shoe or a sandal? He said to me: Does anyone do חליצה with a soft shoe?! The Torah said "his נעל," not "his מנעל."
steps.whatsHappening: The story from the ברייתא continues. The elder reports that רבי יהודה בן בתירא would not use a soft shoe for חליצה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The elder reports that רבי יהודה בן בתירא would not use a מנעל for חליצה. He reads the פסוק's word נעלו as a sandal-type shoe, which leaves out a מנעל. The גמרא in step 10 frames this ברייתא as a dispute about using a מנעל לכתחילה, so this is the side that says not to use one from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: A sandal made of hard leather
"His shoe", the word the Torah uses for חליצה

phrases.english: He said to me:
I saw that he conducted חליצה many times.
With a soft shoe or with a sandal?
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי asking. The words "I asked him" are left out but understood.

phrases.english: He said to me: Does anyone do חליצה with a soft shoe?!
But the Torah said: "his shoe (נעלו)"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:9. Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: and not "his soft shoe (מנעלו)".

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לִי: רָאִיתִי שֶׁחָלַץ הַרְבֵּה פְּעָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the elder's answer to רבי יוסי's question from step 11.
steps.raayaObject: Shows that a תנא, רבי יהודה בן בתירא, would not use a מנעל for חליצה לכתחילה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the elder of נציבין and רבי יהודה בן בתירא.

steps.title: רבי יוסי asks how רבי מאיר could call it valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי challenges the elder: if a מנעל is not valid, why did רבי מאיר rule that a חליצה done with a מנעל is valid?
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: If so, what did רבי מאיר see that made him say: if she did חליצה with a soft shoe, her חליצה is valid?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי pushes back against the elder's strict view. He points to רבי מאיר, who ruled that a מנעל works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the dispute among תנאים that step 10 promised. The elder's side says a מנעל should not be used for חליצה. רבי מאיר's ruling says a חליצה done with a מנעל works.

keyTerms.meaning: What did he see? (What was his reason?)

phrases.english: I said to him: If so,
what did רבי מאיר see, that he said:
If she did חליצה with a soft shoe, her חליצה is valid?!
phrases.notes: These are the exact words of our משנה, credited here to רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַרְתִּי לוֹ: אִם כֵּן, מָה רָאָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the elder's claim in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The elder's view that no one does חליצה with a מנעל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר clearly ruled that a חליצה done with a מנעל is valid, so the elder's view cannot be the only one.

steps.title: רבי יעקב: רבי מאיר allowed a soft shoe even from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב reports in רבי מאיר's name that one may use a מנעל for חליצה even לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב says in his name: One may do חליצה with a soft shoe even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב makes רבי מאיר's view clear: a מנעל may be used even לכתחילה, not only after the fact as the משנה's wording might suggest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the dispute among תנאים is clear. רבי יהודה בן בתירא would not use a מנעל from the start. רבי מאיר, as רבי יעקב reports, allows it even לכתחילה. The משנה's past-tense wording does not limit him, just as step 9 explained. These two sides match רבה's and רב יוסף's versions.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start; as the proper first choice

steps.whatToRemember: The תנאים argue about using a מנעל לכתחילה. רבי יהודה בן בתירא (as the elder reports) would not use one from the start. רבי מאיר (as רבי יעקב reports) allows it even לכתחילה. These match רבה's and רב יוסף's versions of רב.

phrases.english: רבי יעקב says in his name:
One may do חליצה with a soft shoe even from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר מִשְּׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא by showing that רבי מאיר allows a מנעל even לכתחילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יעקב's report of רבי מאיר, a מנעל may be used for חליצה even לכתחילה.

steps.title: Why would anyone forbid a soft shoe from the start?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the view that a מנעל should not be used לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says a soft shoe should not be used from the start, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finished, and the גמרא now asks its own question. It is setting up a search for the reason behind the middle view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view that forbids a מנעל לכתחילה is puzzling. If a מנעל works after the fact, why not use it from the start? The גמרא wants the logic that would explain this split.

phrases.english: And the one who says: not from the start,
what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר לְכַתְּחִלָּה לָא, מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the ברייתא's report to asking for the reasoning behind one of its views.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a מנעל would be valid after the fact but not allowed לכתחילה.

steps.title: A first try: the straps sit on top of the shoe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a מנעל is a problem because its straps sit on top of the shoe's upper part, which is "on top of on top" of the foot. The Torah says the shoe must be "from on" the foot.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because the upper part of the shoe is on the foot, and the straps are on top of what is on top, and the Torah said "from on" the foot, not "from on top of what is on top".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible reason for the middle view. A מנעל has a layer of straps over the shoe, so part of it is not directly "on" the foot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is based on the פסוק's word מעל ("from on"). The shoe must sit directly on the foot. The straps of a מנעל sit on top of another layer, so they are "on top of on top," and that might not count.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that will be tested)
The upper part of the shoe
The straps tied around the shoe
On top of what is on top

phrases.english: If you say it is because the upper part of the shoe is on the foot,
and the straps are on top of what is on top,
and the Torah said: "from on" his foot,
and not "from on top of what is on top".

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוְיָא פַּנְתָּא מֵעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Maybe a מנעל is a problem because its straps are not directly on the foot, while the Torah says "מעל רגלו".

steps.title: That reason would forbid it even after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first answer. If the Torah itself excludes a מנעל, it should not work even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should not work even after the fact!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the suggested reason proves too much. It would make a מנעל invalid even בדיעבד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A reason taken from the פסוק makes the act invalid from the Torah. But the view we are explaining says a מנעל is valid after the fact, so this cannot be its reason.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not why a מנעל is invalid. The question is why it is valid after the fact but should not be used from the start. Any reason taken from the Torah would make it invalid all the way.

phrases.english: If so,
then even after the fact it should not work either!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ דִּיעֲבַד נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer offered in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the "on top of on top" reason as the explanation for the view that forbids a מנעל לכתחילה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A reason from the Torah would make a מנעל invalid even בדיעבד, which goes against the view being explained.

steps.title: The real reason: a decree because of a torn shoe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ban on using a מנעל לכתחילה is a rabbinic decree. The worry is that someone might use a torn מנעל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree because of a torn soft shoe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. By Torah law a מנעל is fine, but the חכמים said not to use it from the start, because people might come to use a torn one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because this is only a rabbinic precaution, it fits the view that forbids a מנעל לכתחילה. After the fact the חליצה still counts, since from the Torah a whole מנעל is valid. The rule only guards against a torn shoe.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree; a precaution set up by the חכמים

steps.whatToRemember: The view that forbids a מנעל לכתחילה but accepts it בדיעבד rests on a rabbinic decree, made out of concern for a torn מנעל. It is not a Torah-level problem.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in גמרא: when a ruling is "not from the start, but valid after the fact," the reason is often a rabbinic precaution, not a Torah-level problem.

phrases.english: It is a decree because of a torn soft shoe.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם מִנְעָל מְרוּפָּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason from step 16 with a reason that fits.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban on using a מנעל לכתחילה is a rabbinic decree, out of concern that someone might use a torn מנעל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A מנעל is valid by Torah law. Only a rabbinic precaution against torn shoes keeps some from using it לכתחילה.

steps.title: Another reason for the decree: a half shoe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a second reason for the rabbinic ban on using a מנעל לכתחילה: someone might use a shoe that covers only half the foot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or else, the decree is because of a half shoe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second possible reason why the רבנן said not to use a מנעל לכתחילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18 the worry was a torn מנעל. Here the worry is a חצי מנעל, a soft shoe that covers only half the foot, which is not good for חליצה. The ban is still only a rabbinic decree; only the reason behind it is different.

keyTerms.meaning: A half shoe, a soft shoe that covers only part of the foot
A rabbinic decree made to keep people from a mistake

phrases.english: Alternatively,
it is because of a half shoe.
phrases.notes: The words 'it is a decree' are left out here, but the גמרא means them, carried over from step 18.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי מִשּׁוּם חֲצִי מִנְעָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second reason for the same rabbinic decree described in step 18
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban on a מנעל לכתחילה is a decree in case someone uses a half shoe

steps.title: רב would prefer a tight Arab sandal
steps.stepSummary: רב says that if he had not seen his uncle do חליצה with a laced sandal, he would only use a tight-fitting Arab sandal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: If I had not seen my beloved uncle do חליצה with a sandal that has laces, I would only do חליצה with an Arab sandal, which fits more tightly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב shares what kind of sandal he thinks is best for חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב leaned toward a sandal that sits tightly on the foot, so that taking it off is a real act. Because he saw his uncle use a laced sandal, he accepted that a laced sandal is also fine.

keyTerms.meaning: My beloved one; רב's name for his uncle

phrases.english: Rav said:
If I had not seen my beloved one
phrases.notes: 'My beloved' is how רב refers to his uncle, רבי חייה.

phrases.english: perform חליצה with a sandal that has laces,
I would not perform חליצה
except with a sandal of Arabs,
which is more tight-fitting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: אִי לָאו דַּחֲמֵיתֵיהּ לְחַבִּיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the מנעל question to which kind of sandal is best for חליצה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tight-fitting sandal is best for חליצה, but a laced sandal is also acceptable, as רב saw his uncle use one

steps.title: Tying an extra strap on our sandal
steps.stepSummary: The local sandal already has a ring, but they still tie a strap onto it so the חליצה will be done in the best way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our sandal, even though it has a ring, we still tie a strap to it, so that her חליצה will be done in the best way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes the practice in its own time: they add a strap to the sandal used for חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows רב's idea that the shoe should be tight. Even a sandal that already has a ring gets an extra strap, so the shoe stays firmly on and the יבמה must really work to take it off.

keyTerms.meaning: A ring or loop on the sandal

phrases.english: And this sandal of ours,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִית בֵּיהּ חוּמַרְתָּא,
phrases.english: even though it has a ring on it,
we tie a strap to it,
so that her חליצה will be of the highest standard.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי דִּידַן, אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִית בֵּיהּ חוּמַרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts רב's preference for a tight sandal into everyday practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An extra strap is tied onto the sandal so the חליצה is done in the best way
steps.whatToRemember: For חליצה the shoe should sit tightly on the foot, so they go out of their way to tighten it.

steps.title: The יבמה is free once most of the heel is out
steps.stepSummary: After a memory sign, רב יהודה quotes רב: the יבמה is free to marry anyone once most of the heel has come out of the shoe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory sign: Release, יבמה, sandal. רב יהודה said in רב's name: A יבמה is free to marry anyone once most of the heel is out of the shoe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short memory sign for a set of teachings of רב יהודה in רב's name, and then gives the first one: how much of the shoe must come off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full foot does not have to leave the shoe. Once most of the heel is out, the חליצה is done and the יבמה may marry someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign to help remember a list of teachings
Making the יבמה free to marry
Literally 'to the market'; to marry any man
When most of the heel slips out of the shoe

phrases.english: A memory sign: Release, yevama, sandal.
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The release of a yevama to marry anyone
happens with the removal of most of the heel.

steps.triggerLanguage: סִימַן: הַתָּרַת יְבָמָה סַנְדָּל. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new set of teachings, beginning with how much of the shoe must come off
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once most of the heel is out of the shoe, the יבמה is free to marry anyone

steps.title: A ברייתא about most of the foot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב with a ברייתא: if the straps came untied, or most of the foot slipped out, the חליצה is not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: If the straps of a מנעל or a סנדל came untied, or if he slipped out most of his foot, her חליצה is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to argue with רב's rule about most of the heel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא talks about the man himself slipping 'most of the foot' out, before the יבמה finished taking the shoe off. That makes it sound as if the point that counts is most of the foot, not most of the heel. This seems to argue with רב, and the answer comes in step 25.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of the foot slipped out

steps.confusionAlert: The problem in the ברייתא is not that the shoe came off. It is that it came off without the יבמה doing it. The challenge to רב comes from how much of the foot the ברייתא talks about.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If the straps of a shoe or sandal came untied,
or if he slipped out most of his foot,
her חליצה is disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הוּתְּרוּ רְצוּעוֹת מִנְעָל וְסַנְדָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's rule from step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that the יבמה is free once most of the heel is out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats 'most of the foot' as the point where the removal is done. That suggests most of the heel is not enough, which goes against רב.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא closely to challenge רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an inference from the ברייתא. If she pulls off most of the foot, the חליצה works, but that seems to say most of the heel is not enough, against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא calls it invalid only because he pulled the shoe off. So if she had pulled it off, her חליצה would be valid. But the ברייתא speaks of 'most of the foot.' That means most of the foot, yes; most of the heel, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the challenge it started in step 23. It reads between the lines of the ברייתא to show it seems to argue with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the חליצה is invalid when most of the foot came out by itself or through him. So when she removes most of the foot, it should be valid. But רב said most of the heel is enough, and the ברייתא's wording, 'most of the foot,' sounds like a bigger amount.

phrases.english: The reason [it is invalid] is that he pulled it off,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the brother-in-law. The ברייתא from step 23 spoke of the foot slipping out without her doing it.

phrases.english: but if she pulled it off,
her חליצה is valid.
Most of the foot, yes;
most of the heel, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּשָׁמַט הוּא, הָא שָׁמְטָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out exactly how the ברייתא quoted in step 23 contradicts רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling (step 22) that most of the heel coming out is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies that validity depends on 'most of the foot,' which is more than 'most of the heel.'

steps.title: Most of the foot means most of the heel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'most of the foot' and 'most of the heel' are the same thing. The heel is called 'the foot' because the whole weight of the leg rests on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. 'Most of the foot' is the same as 'most of the heel.' Why is it called 'most of the foot'? Because the whole weight of the leg presses down on the heel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. It shows the ברייתא's words really mean the same thing as רב's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no argument at all. The ברייתא's 'foot' is just another name for the heel. The heel carries all the weight of the leg, so it counts as the main part of the foot.
steps.whatToRemember: For רב, once most of the heel is out of the shoe, the חליצה is done. The ברייתא's 'most of the foot' means the same thing.

phrases.english: No: 'most of the foot'
is the same as 'most of the heel.'
And why do they call it 'most of the foot'?
Because the whole weight of the leg
presses down on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא: הַיְינוּ רוֹב הָרֶגֶל, הַיְינוּ רוֹב הֶעָקֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term: the two phrases mean the same thing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Most of the foot' means a bigger amount than 'most of the heel.'
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Most of the foot' is just a name for most of the heel, because the heel carries the leg's weight.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports רבי ינאי
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא supports רבי ינאי. He holds that the woman must both untie the shoe and pull it off herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי ינאי, who said: Whether he untied it and she pulled it off, or she untied it and he pulled it off, her חליצה is invalid. It works only when she unties it and she pulls it off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא from step 23 backs up a ruling of רבי ינאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא invalidated the חליצה when the man had a hand in getting the shoe off. That fits רבי ינאי, who says every part of the removal must be done by her. If he unties or he pulls off, it does not count.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: the woman herself must untie and remove the shoe.

phrases.english: This supports רבי ינאי,
for רבי ינאי said:
Whether he untied it and she pulled it off,
or she untied it and he pulled it off,
her חליצה is invalid,
unless she unties it and she pulls it off.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 23 for a new purpose: to support רבי ינאי.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ינאי's rule that the woman must both untie and remove the shoe.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא invalidating חליצה when the foot came out without her doing it.

steps.title: What if she tears or burns the shoe?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי asks whether tearing or burning the shoe counts as חליצה. Is the point to uncover the foot, or to take the shoe off? The question stays unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי asked: If she tore the shoe, what is the law? If she burned it, what is the law? Do we need the foot to be uncovered, and here it is? Or do we need the shoe to be taken off, and here it was not? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי asks about unusual ways of getting the shoe off the foot. The גמרא explains what the question depends on and leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing or burning leaves the foot bare, but nobody actually slid the shoe off. If the מצוה is about uncovering the foot, it works. If it is about the act of removing, it does not. No answer is found, so it ends with תיקו.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to see חליצה: uncovering the foot, or removing the shoe. Tearing or burning shows the difference, and the question is left open.

phrases.english: רבי ינאי asked:
If she tore it, what is the law?
If she burned it, what is the law?
Do we need uncovering of the foot,
and here it is?
Or perhaps we need taking off [the shoe],
and here it is missing?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי: קְרָעַתְהוּ, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another question from רבי ינאי about how the shoe must come off.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does tearing or burning the shoe count as valid חליצה?

steps.title: Two shoes, one on top of the other
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה asks רבה what the law is when the man is wearing two shoes, one over the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה asked רבה: If there are two shoes, one on top of the other, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins: how does חליצה work with a double shoe? The גמרא will first ask what exact case is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question is related to רבי ינאי's. When one shoe is over another, removing a shoe and uncovering the foot may not happen together.

keyTerms.meaning: one on top of the other

phrases.english: רבי נחמיה asked רבה:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי מִנְעָלִים זֶה עַל גַּב זֶה, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: Two shoes, one on top of the other: what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה מֵרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question on a similar theme: what counts as removal.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is חליצה valid when the man wears two shoes, one over the other?

steps.title: Removing only the outer shoe obviously fails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case is meant. If she took off only the outer shoe, that clearly does not work. The Torah says 'from on his foot,' not 'from on what is on his foot.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say she pulled off the upper shoe and the lower one stays on, that cannot be the question. The Torah says 'from on [his foot],' not 'from on what is on [his foot].'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is narrowing down the question. It rules out a case that is too obvious to ask about, which prepares the real case in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק requires the shoe to come off the foot itself. Removing the outer shoe only takes a shoe off another shoe. So that case is obviously invalid, and רבי נחמיה must have meant something else.

keyTerms.meaning: from on top of what is on top

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say she pulled off the upper one
and the lower one stays on,
the Torah said 'from on [his foot],'
and not 'from on what is on [his foot].'

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי: אִילֵּימָא דִּשְׁלַפְתֵּיהּ לְעִילַּאי וְקָאֵי תַּתַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies רבי נחמיה's question by ruling out the obvious case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which exact case of two shoes is רבי נחמיה asking about?

steps.title: The real case: inner shoe off, torn outer shoe still on
steps.stepSummary: The question is about a case where she tore the outer shoe and pulled off the inner one, while the torn outer shoe stays on. Is removal enough, or must the foot be uncovered?
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the question is about this case: she tore the upper shoe and pulled off the lower one, and the upper one stays on. What is the law? Do we need removal, and here we have it? Or perhaps we need the foot uncovered, and here it is not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the real case behind רבי נחמיה's question. It shows that it depends on the same two sides as רבי ינאי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a shoe really was pulled off the foot, but the foot is still covered by the torn outer shoe. This is the opposite of tearing or burning, where the foot is bare but nothing was pulled off. So this case tests the other side of the same issue.

keyTerms.meaning: it is needed only for (this case)

steps.confusionAlert: This is the reverse of רבי ינאי's case. There the foot was uncovered with no removal. Here there was removal, but the foot is still covered.

phrases.english: No, it is needed for this case:
where she tore the upper one
and pulled off the lower one,
and the upper one stays on. What is the law?
Do we need taking off, and here we have it?
Or perhaps we need uncovering of the foot,
and here it is missing?
